> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 91f6a0b4e58e02e25e2921a33f8f8690ec1b2937` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dddf84560fe2234c3d15b73f604a68ccf42ecc87` — the merge of head `986b2d01c7f40a5fdcda0d3d6953c8e338d718c4` into base `91f6a0b4e58e02e25e2921a33f8f8690ec1b2937`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dddf84560fe2234c3d15b73f604a68ccf42ecc87 && git checkout dddf84560fe2234c3d15b73f604a68ccf42ecc87
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 91f6a0b4e58e02e25e2921a33f8f8690ec1b2937 986b2d01c7f40a5fdcda0d3d6953c8e338d718c4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 91f6a0b4e58e02e25e2921a33f8f8690ec1b2937 && git merge --no-ff 986b2d01c7f40a5fdcda0d3d6953c8e338d718c4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 91f6a0b4e58e02e25e2921a33f8f8690ec1b2937
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 91f6a0b4e58e02e25e2921a33f8f8690ec1b2937` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `986b2d01c7f40a5fdcda0d3d6953c8e338d718c4`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #29396 (body, the triage, both claims, the dev's report 6582986079); the source record 6577747588 on PR #29270 (S4, open question 2); PR #29508's body, its file list (5 files) and the net diff against its merge base `6af3d295` (the merge of `origin/main` adds no file to it); the cited code on the head, read only: `namedBaseCloseSubject` and `judgeOverrideWrite` (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`), `ensureCustomizationPackage` and `customizationPairEnsureRefusal` (`protocol-customization-package.ts`), `isWritablePackage` (`package-writability.ts`, `protocol-package-scope.ts`), `migratePackagelessOverlays` (`protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts`), the pending `.changeset/28905-named-base-overlay-write-closed.md`, and `packages/cli/package.json`'s `exports`; the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The carry goes through the administrator's doors, in the administrator's order.** `carryIntoPair` calls (a) `pairs.ensure(base)`, wired to the protocol service's own `ensureCustomizationPackage` (the body of `POST /packages/:id/ensure-customization`, the same in-process call `migratePackagelessOverlays` makes), then (b) the ceremony's existing `door.save`, which is `protocol.saveMetaItem` with `packageId` set to the pair id the ensure door answered and the body carrying `overrides: { package: base, basedOn }`. Both are the doors an administrator's pair save meets; neither is bypassed, re-implemented or pre-judged in the cli. Every refusal either door gives is caught and either blocks or falls to main's save, which the door judges again. Right.
2. **`basedOn` is the value the door names.** The cli reads the installed base's `manifest.version` off `engine.registry.getPackage(base)`, the same read `namedBaseCloseSubject` makes for the fix it names (`basedOn = registry.getPackage(base)?.manifest?.version`) and `os migrate packageless-overlays` records (`baseVersionOf`). The D2 gate records `basedOn` and never judges it (`judgeOverrideWrite`'s docblock); the schema gate requires its presence, which the port guarantees (an empty or non-string version throws, and the carry falls back). A served body that already declares the base keeps its own `basedOn` (the pair's override as served); every other body takes the installed version. Right, and pinned: the integration case stores `{ package: 'com.example.wdpair', basedOn: '1.4.0' }`.
3. **It never writes into the base, nor into a writable package's view through the pair.** The pair branch saves only with `packageId: pair.packageId`, the ensure door's answer (`BASE.custom`); it cannot name the base. A writable package returns `carried: false` with no refusal before any ensure, and its view is saved in place exactly as on main (pinned: `['crm_lead.intake', 'pkg_a', false, undefined]`, `ensured: []`). The only save naming a read-only base is the fallback, which is main's save, judged by the door (item 6). Right.
4. **No pair is ensured for a package that is not read-only.** Three guards, all the server's: `readOnly` is `!isWritablePackage(engine, id)`, ADR-0070 D2's one predicate that the save door and the ensure door both use; the ensure door itself refuses a writable base (`409 ... is writable: customize it directly`); a package-less view (`servedPackageOf` null) never enters the branch, and a served view whose package is a pair is writable (the ensure door installs it with no `system`/`cloud` scope), so it is saved in place. Ablation 2 in the PR body (writability ignored, the writable case red) is the dev's pin of this. Right.
5. **A re-run is a no-op.** The carry only writes where `anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn` finds the served body still serving the form open; after the carry, the env-wide list serves the pair's override at the base's slot, withdrawn, so `closing` is empty. Pinned twice: the unit case runs a second apply with a fresh ledger (no checkpoint) and the saves stay at 1; the integration case re-boots with the package service and reads `open: []` from the list the anonymous doors judge by, then a second `--apply` reads `checkpointed` with the stored rows byte-equal. Right.
6. **The fallback never bypasses a refusal the door would give.** The fallback is `door.save('view', name, body, { packageId })` on the unmutated body, main's call verbatim; the door judges it afresh. `namedBaseCloseSubject` closes the base-named save exactly where the pair can take the declared write (shipper, pair id, `customizationPairEnsureRefusal` none, a version, the D2 gate admits); where the pair branch fails for those same reasons, the door admits the base-named save, as on main; where it fails for any other reason, the door refuses and the step blocks, the pair's refusal now named beside the door's. There is no path where the cli writes something the door did not admit. Read case by case against main: every input main carried, the head carries (into the pair, or by main's save); every input main blocked, the head carries into the pair or still blocks. Right.
7. **The `single` posture skip still holds.** `heldByOrganization` is read before the pair branch, unchanged; a view whose `name + package` key an organization row holds is skipped under `single` before any ensure or save. The observed side effect (a package-less organization row of a shipped name promoted beside the pair's override, both withdrawn) is main's behaviour and `os migrate packageless-overlays`' job; the dev filed it as out of scope, correctly.
8. **Derived, not asked: the readOnly set is wider than the close's set.** `!isWritablePackage` also covers an installed `system`/`cloud`-scope package that is not a booted code package, which `overlayBaseShippers` (the close's reading of "packaged") does not. For such a view the carry now goes into the pair where main's base-named save may have been admitted. That is the spec'd place (ADR-0146 D1, D3: the pair holds the changes to "a read-only base — one provided by code or an installed app"), the ensure door admits it, and nothing refused before is written; not a defect.
9. **Derived, not asked: an ensured pair can survive a fallback.** Where the ensure door creates the pair and the door then refuses the declared save into it, the fallback may carry by main's save, leaving an empty pair installed. That is the ensure door's ordinary product, the same one an administrator's ensure leaves, and it changes no later verdict (the close already judged the pair ensurable). Nit, no action.
10. **The command wiring stays inside the card.** `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts` gains one import (`isWritablePackage`, an existing export of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`), one optional member on the local `protocol` service type, and the `pairs:` block. The apply module is ports-only, so the ensure door is reachable only from the command; the card's Ask (ensure the pair, then save declared) cannot be met without this wiring. It touches nothing on the claim's ⛔ list (no door, close predicate, `protocol.ts`, `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, `packages/spec/**`, error code), and the dev declared it as a deviation. Right.
11. **Accept sets and public surface.** No door, gate, error code or request shape changes: the diff touches only `packages/cli` and `.changeset`. The new exports `CustomizationPairPort`, `protocolCustomizationPairs` and the optional `ApplyOptions.pairs` live in `src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts`, which none of `@objectstack/cli`'s published entries (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`) re-exports; they are internal. Absent `pairs`, the carry is main's code path unchanged. Right.
12. **Tests.** Five unit cases (read-only carried and re-run, writable in place, unensurable pair blocks, refused pair save blocks, the admitted-fallback control) and one real-command integration case. No existing assertion changed; the helper gained two pass-through options. The card's "pins with a read-only package's view and a writable one" is met.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29396-withdrawal-carry-into-pair.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. The diff publishes a behaviour fix in one command (a step that stopped on a blocker now completes through the spec'd door) and no published API surface. `patch` matches.
- `Clause-②: no` is right, in the PR body and the changeset. Nothing accepted on main is refused on the head (① 6: every input main carried, the head carries), and no published surface widens (① 11: the new names are not reachable from any `exports` entry; no door's accept set moves). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no metadata type, schema or protocol method changes.
- The changeset's note that the manual step in the pending `28905-named-base-overlay-write-closed.md` (line 38) is no longer needed when the pair can be ensured is accurate, and that changeset is untouched; both are unreleased, so they ship together.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (the fallback), answered A.** The card's "otherwise it keeps the blocker" names today's behaviour, and today's behaviour is: the door blocks where it refuses and carries where it admits. Option B would make the cli refuse a carry the door admits, a new refusal in a published command that main completes, which is a narrowing this card was not dispatched to make and would turn `Clause-②: no` false. A keeps every case the close left open exactly as on main and blocks wherever the door refuses (① 6). Answered A, no change.
- **Deviation: file surface widened to the command wiring and a new integration file.** Accepted (① 10): both are in `packages/cli`, both are required by the Ask, neither is on the claim's ⛔ list.
- **Deviation: merge of `origin/main` (9 commits, none in `packages/cli`).** Accepted: a merge, not a rebase; the net diff against the merge base is the 5 files above.
- **Deviation: 5 gates exited 3 on missing prerequisites, then 0 on a rerun** (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` after its fixture commit was fetched; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-walk-parity` after the cli dist was built; `check:i18n-coverage` after packages and examples were built). Accepted: exit 3 is the gates' "prerequisite not met" answer, not a verdict, and each rerun after supplying the named prerequisite is the gate's real measurement; the derived set reconciled 62/62 with 0 NOT-MEASURED. The two cli unit files that said "packages/cli is not built" are the same class and passed after the build. The verdicts of record are the head's check-runs below, not the local runs.
- **Out-of-scope finding (package-less organization row beside the pair's override under `single`).** Existing behaviour, owned by `os migrate packageless-overlays`; not filed, correctly. No card owed.
- **Security findings: none.** Concur: the in-process ensure and save are the same calls `os migrate packageless-overlays` makes, under the ceremony's existing actor.
- **Check-runs on the head, as read at 2026-11-02T17:11Z:** 48 runs, all completed: 35 success, 13 skipped (the opt-in and path-filtered jobs: the 18.x upgrade harness, Build & E2E UI, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Type Check UI, UI Published Artifacts, the packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, the schedule gate and the two matrix templates), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Green among them: Test Core (all 8 shards and the aggregate), Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint lane including PM dispatch-gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none. Nit: ① 9 (an ensured pair can survive a fallback), no action.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [41489549492](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/41489549492) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (2/8)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/41489549492/job/125429690485)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```
  @objectstack/spec:test:repo:  FAIL   repo  scripts/strictness-ledger-doc.test.ts > the ledger and the generated counts agree > is checked in current — every shard on disk equals a fresh render, and no
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/spec:test:repo: AssertionError: expected Map{ …(14) } to deeply equal Map{ …(14) }
  @objectstack/spec:test:repo:  FAIL   repo  scripts/strictness-ledger-doc.test.ts > the ledger and the generated counts agree > the read-time totals equal the sums of the shards' own rows
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/spec:test:repo: AssertionError: expected 'untriaged: 1293 object site(s) across…' to be 'untriaged: 1292 object site(s) across…' // Object.is equality
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

- `scripts/strictness-ledger-doc.test.ts` — 24h 内已弹出 **2 个 PR**（#29100、#29508），但它们同属 **1 条投机栈** ⇒ **1 次独立命中**。汇总 issue：#29524（新建）
- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。

- 过去 24h 队列共有 4 个失败构建（不含本次）。
